correctness.rationale: The cases exhaust all Hilbert partial isometries. The external 2022 scalar-plus-compact modulus theorem yields two independent orthonormal-sequence lower bounds, max(alpha,|1-alpha|)>=1/2. The unitary extension attains this bound when both defects are infinite. With finite cokernel, a less-than-one perturbation has an invertible initial-to-final compression; its graph makes the approximant kernel infinite, contradicting the cited noncompact finite-kernel theorem. Compact approximants are at distance >=1, and zero attains 1. The first case is AN by compactness or finite-kernel intersection. All limits, boundaries and quantifiers are handled without numerical extrapolation.

value.rationale: Distance to a distinguished closed operator class is a natural quantitative refinement of the 2022 qualitative characterization. The exactly attained trichotomy detects a cokernel obstruction that membership and positive modulus do not capture. The explicit projection/coisometry pair with identical modulus but sharp distances 1/2 and 1 makes the structural distinction meaningful, not a routine restatement of the published membership criterion.
